# Milestone M1: one-arm bench kit in two steps (generated by `python -m rnd.m1_kit`)

**Step 1 (one joint: GIM protocol + safety chain): $1,214 + 15% = $1,397.** **Step 2 (the rest of the arm, today's plan): $1,343 + 15% = $1,545.** Whole kit $2,941 with contingency (the previous list: $1,945, with a 10 A supply, no safety-board logic, a motors-only hold A and none of the C1/M1/M7 fix parts).

| Scenario (with contingency) | Step 2 | Whole kit |
|---|---|---|
| **Today's plan**: GIM6010 at pitch + elbow, approved inline roll | $1,545 | **$2,941** |
| Hold A yes (D20, with its drive parts) + inline roll | $1,646 | $3,042 |
| Fallback: belt roll (hold B no), GIM6010 at pitch + elbow | $1,260 | $2,657 |

Hold A (D20) costs **+$101** against the GIM6010 lines (up to +$329 at the dearest motor listing); the inline roll +$285 against the belt roll (up to +$362). Step 1: 9 of 23 lines priced from retailer snapshots, 14 ESTIMATE. Everything except the two supplies, the stand, the test lever and the catch is reused in the arm and the robot.

**Why two steps (Fable review 2026-11-27, verdict):** no GIM can be commanded until its CAN protocol is known, the arm mixes three SteadyWin drivers (docs/sw/gim_protocol_notes.md), and the arm CAD has fixes to land before printing (C1 insert pull-out, C3 rear cap, M1 inline boss/stops, M5 belt centres). Step 1 settles the protocol and the safety chain on one real GIM with only one GIM bought; the bench supply and the safety board are most of its cost and any arm needs them; Step 2 is bought when its exit criteria are met ([M1_READINESS.md](M1_READINESS.md)). **No extra GIM6010s in Step 1.**

**What Step 1 proves on hardware:** the SDC104's CAN protocol (`python -m sw.gim_discover`: MIT / impedance mode or not), enable, zero-gain and impedance control, the drive's torque limit in flash and its CAN timeout; the safety board (pre-charge, one-shot discharge, clamp, contactor, watchdog at 25 ms, e-stop → no torque ≤ 50 ms) with a real drive; torque constant and friction on a lever bolted to the output; the collision trip on one joint; the motor case temperature rise at rated torque on the lever; insert pull-out, the bolted-flange coupon and the drive-stub coupon (C45 stub on the GIM output, 8 × M3 × 6).

**Step-1 exit criterion added 2026-11-27 (software track: determinism, the Asimov sim2real lessons): soak test.** `python -m sw.soak --joints yaw,wpitch --hours 2` on the Step-1 rig. A sysid fit at the start (bring-up step `sysid`, sw/sysid.py: Coulomb + viscous friction, effective torque constant, backlash, command → response latency → sw/config/actuators_<serial>.yaml), then 2 h of 0.25 Hz cyclic motion at ≈ 50 % rated torque (2 kg at the 0.3 m lever end on the yaw stage, 0.5 kg at the wrist), then the sysid fit again with the drives hot. **Pass:** Coulomb drift ≤ 20 %, viscous ≤ 25 %, torque constant ≤ 5 %, backlash growth ≤ 0.1°, latency mean ≤ +0.5 ms and p95 ≤ +2 ms; no supervisor stop, no CAN bus-off, no new Pi throttle / under-voltage flag (`vcgencmd get_throttled`), zero implausible (corrupted) CAN frames, loop jitter p99 < 1 ms, CPU < 80 °C (rehearsed on the virtual bench: a stable drive passes, a drive whose friction drifts with temperature fails; docs/sw/sim2real_bench.md). The lever measurements of the torque constant and friction above are this step. **Proposed Step-1 line (lead to add in rnd/m1_kit.py):** one Waveshare 2-CH CAN FD HAT ($46.99) to measure SPI-CAN (MCP2518FD) against the two gs_usb adapters on the same bus ([can_interface_note.md](sw/can_interface_note.md)).

**What Step 2 proves:** the whole arm: belts and the D13 v3 stages, the bolted cartridges, the balancer (A9), the inline roll, hand sag (R2b) and, if the encoder mounts and node firmware exist by then (Fable M3), hand accuracy; the fin-ray grasp; CAN timing (SW1).

## Questions for the seller (send as one message now; they gate Step 2's motors)

1. **GIM8108-8, 24 V:** we run a 24 V bus (6S Li-ion, 25.2 V full; our regen clamp switches on at 26.4 V and holds it ≤ 27.3 V, absolute max 28 V). Which driver version of the GIM8108-8 (SDC104, GDZ468, GDS68?) do you ship, and is it specified for 24 V? Please give rated torque, rated speed, no-load speed and continuous current at 24 V (listings quote 48 V). Price and lead time for 2 now (4 later).
2. **GIM8108-8 drawing:** installation drawing with frame diameter and height, output-flange bolt pattern (hole count, PCD, thread, depth) and housing / rear mounting pattern, and the connector position.
3. **GIM8108-36 (SDC303, 24 V):** which face is the output; the output flange material and the dowel-hole depth; reducer **backlash** (listings say 15 arcmin: measured how?); frame and connector position (we have the Ø96 × 57 drawing).
4. **GIM8108-36 output bearing:** please give the **bearing type** (deep-groove, angular-contact pair, crossed-roller?) and its **radial, axial and tilting-moment ratings** (static and dynamic, and where along the output they are referenced). Our two load cases at the output flange (rnd/joints.py, M1 roll support, Astra review): **with our rear 61806 support, ≈ 1,413 N radial in service and 3,130 N radial at a fault** (a collision or a stall, including misalignment); **without it, a tilting moment of 36.4 N·m in service and 137 N·m at a fault**. One listing gives 1000 N radial / 250 N axial: please confirm, and say which of the two cases the bearing carries. Price with the SDC303 driver and lead time.
5. **CAN protocol manual** for the SDC104 (GIM6010-8), SDC303 (GIM8108-36) and the GIM8108-8's driver: frame formats; is the MIT / impedance mode (position, velocity, kp, kd, torque feed-forward) the default or selected in the tool, and its float ranges; how to set the node ID and the feedback ID; 1 Mbit/s; a **CAN-command timeout** (the drive disables itself when commands stop) and its unit; a torque / current-limit parameter **saved to flash**; encoder zero (is the output angle kept over a power cycle?); status and error codes; under/over-voltage behaviour. **Is it the same protocol on all three drivers?**
6. **GIM6010-8:** confirm the unit is the 24 V **SDC104** version (not a 48 V listing), with its installation drawing and which face carries the housing mounting holes (rear or output face: our cartridge cap depends on it, Fable C3).

Ask Damiao (or the DM-J4310 reseller) separately: the V1.1 output bearing's allowable radial load and moment.

## Check before paying / on arrival

- GIM6010-8: the **24 V SDC104** version; DM-J4310-2EC: **V1.1** (ask for the output bearing's radial / moment rating: the wrist pitch sees ≈ 0.9 N·m bending, more with the basket hook); STS3215: the **12 V C018**.
- SE-1000-24: the 24 V model (not -12 / -48); check the overload mode on its datasheet (constant-current limiting) and set 24.0–25.2 V.
- Aluminium HTD 5M pulleys (Step 2): 15 mm belt, **12 H7 bore with a 4 mm keyway**, set screw on the key.
- Drive stub (D26): measure the GIM output's bolt circle, pilot and output-bearing position on the Step-1 motor (coupon_motor) and set belt_stage.STUB / MOTOR['out_pcd'] before quoting the stubs from the STEP; the 6001 seat k6, the pulley seat h6 with a 4 mm keyway.
- Crush sleeves (W8c, D26): measure each printed stack; pitch / yaw sleeves turned 42CrMo4+QT (R_p0.2 ≥ 750 MPa on the certificate) to print − 0.05 mm; clevis / rear sleeves cut from the E235+C tube sticks and faced in the jig to print − 0.05 ± 0.02 (micrometer).
- Vishay NH-50 (not RH-50) for the three clamp resistors: the part number starts NH050; the pre-charge and dummy-load resistors stay RH-50.
- Heat-set inserts: the short M4 (5.7 mm) the flange calls for; the long 8.1 mm ones don't fit the 6 mm flange.

**Order of work:** build and test the safety board (electrical.md, bench tests before any motor) → protocol discovery on the GIM6010-8 → bring-up on the Step-1 rig (`--joints yaw,wpitch`) → coupons (insert pull-out, bolted flange + drive-stub coupon: [COUPONS.md](COUPONS.md)) → Step 2.
